Memory complexity is minimal, requiring only timer registers and ADC readings [S1].

The claim states that the memory complexity is minimal and requires 'timer registers and ADC readings'. While the evidence confirms the use of timer registers (Arduino Nano Timer 1) and analog joysticks (which typically involve ADC), it also explicitly mentions the use of an 'ultrasonic range sensor (hc-sr04)' for the distance-controlled method. Ultrasonic sensors typically require digital I/O (trigger and echo pins) rather than just ADC readings. Furthermore, the surface detection method uses a light detector with an op-amp circuit, which may involve ADC, but the claim's assertion that the complexity is 'minimal' and limited to those specific components ignores the digital requirements of the ultrasonic sensor and the additional hardware (dichroic optics, op-amp) mentioned. More importantly, the evidence does not discuss 'memory complexity' at all; it discusses hardware components and functionality. Therefore, the specific claim about memory complexity is not supported by the text.
